claims.title: A stolen long-lived partner key lets an attacker upload as that insurance partner
claims.description: An attacker who obtains the long-lived key for `entity:insurance-partner` can present it on `flow:insurance-partner-to-landing-bucket:push-daily-extract` and authenticate to `store:landing-bucket` as that partner. The flow crosses from the partner network into the landing network, and the key has never been rotated, extending the period in which a compromised key remains usable. Second-order: `process:ingest-scheduler` reads every landed file without verifying its originating partner and triggers processing, so the impostor's upload can enter the transform pipeline and reach `store:claims-warehouse` as apparently partner-supplied claims data.

quotes.text: Each partner has a static key we issued when they onboarded; the keys have not changed since.
An Airflow scheduler running in the landing network wakes up at 02:00, lists the bucket, and reads whatever is there. It does not check that a file came from the partner whose folder it landed in.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because `flow:insurance-partner-to-landing-bucket:push-daily-extract` is a crossing from the externally controlled `boundary:partner-network` and relies on a static key that has never rotated; impact is high because the impersonation can introduce purported partner extracts containing health and PII records into `store:claims-warehouse`, which is confidential and tagged `pii`, `health`, and `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Replace static partner keys with rotatable, scoped partner identities
mitigations.detail: Use a distinct managed credential or certificate for each partner on `flow:insurance-partner-to-landing-bucket:push-daily-extract`, enforce expiry and rotation, and revoke a single partner identity without affecting the others.

mitigations.summary: Bind landed files to the authenticated partner identity
mitigations.detail: Have `store:landing-bucket` or `process:ingest-scheduler` derive the permitted folder and provenance from the verified partner identity, and reject files whose authenticated uploader does not match the claimed partner folder.

claims.title: An attacker can impersonate the scheduler to trigger warehouse transforms if cross-boundary authentication is absent
claims.description: `flow:ingest-scheduler-to-transform-job:trigger-transform` crosses from `boundary:landing-network` to `boundary:warehouse-network` with `authentication: unknown`. If `process:transform-job` does not verify that a trigger came from `process:ingest-scheduler`, an attacker with a foothold in the landing network can impersonate the scheduler and submit transform-run requests naming files to process. Second-order: successful requests cause `process:transform-job` to normalize records and load them through `flow:transform-job-to-claims-warehouse:load-records` into `store:claims-warehouse`, extending the forged scheduler identity into the confidential health and PII warehouse. This draft is conditional on the unstated authentication attribute, not an assertion that authentication is absent.

quotes.text: For each file the scheduler triggers a Spark transform job in the warehouse network. The transform normalizes the records and loads them into BigQuery.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown authentication state because exploiting the crossing requires a foothold in `boundary:landing-network`, while impact is high because impersonated triggers can reach `store:claims-warehouse`, which is confidential and tagged `pii`, `health`, and `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Require verifiable workload authentication for transform triggers
mitigations.detail: Make the authentication on `flow:ingest-scheduler-to-transform-job:trigger-transform` explicit and require mTLS or a short-lived audience-bound workload token that `process:transform-job` validates for the scheduler identity.

mitigations.summary: Authorize and constrain scheduler-triggered jobs
mitigations.detail: Have `process:transform-job` accept requests only from the verified `process:ingest-scheduler` identity and validate that the named input file is an authorized landing-bucket object before running a transform.

claims.title: Leaked partner SFTP keys can plant fraudulent claim extracts
claims.description: An attacker who obtains a long-lived partner key can use `flow:insurance-partner-to-landing-bucket:push-daily-extract` to plant or replace a claims extract in `store:landing-bucket`. `process:ingest-scheduler` reads whatever is present and does not verify that the file originated from the partner whose folder it occupies. Second-order, the scheduler triggers `process:transform-job`, which schema-validates and loads the planted records into `store:claims-warehouse` as normalized claim data.

mitigations.summary: Replace static partner keys with scoped, rotatable identities
mitigations.detail: Use separate short-lived or regularly rotated SFTP credentials for each partner and restrict every identity to its own upload prefix in `store:landing-bucket`.

mitigations.summary: Verify extract provenance before processing
mitigations.detail: Have `process:ingest-scheduler` verify a partner-specific signed manifest and bind the authenticated uploader identity to the expected folder before triggering `process:transform-job`.

mitigations.summary: Validate claim content beyond its schema
mitigations.detail: Add source-specific integrity, ownership, and business-rule validation in `process:transform-job` before loading records into `store:claims-warehouse`.

claims.title: Run requests can be altered in transit if scheduler-to-transform protection is absent
claims.description: `flow:ingest-scheduler-to-transform-job:trigger-transform` crosses from `boundary:landing-network` to `boundary:warehouse-network`, but its `protocol`, `authentication`, and `encryption_in_transit` are all unknown. If transport integrity is not enforced, an attacker with an on-path position can alter the run request naming the file before it reaches `process:transform-job`, causing a different landed file to be processed. Second-order, the transform loads records from the attacker-selected input into `store:claims-warehouse`; this is conditional on the currently unverified transport and caller protections.

Impact is high because altered input selection can corrupt confidential health and PII records in `store:claims-warehouse`, which is also tagged `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Authenticate and integrity-protect transform triggers
mitigations.detail: Use mutually authenticated TLS or an authenticated job-submission API on `flow:ingest-scheduler-to-transform-job:trigger-transform`, with integrity protection from scheduler to transform job.

mitigations.summary: Bind each run request to an approved input artifact
mitigations.detail: Have `process:transform-job` accept a signed, immutable object identifier and verify that its partner, path, and digest match scheduler-approved metadata before processing.

claims.title: Unverified warehouse write authentication may permit claim-record tampering
claims.description: `flow:transform-job-to-claims-warehouse:load-records` performs writes to confidential `store:claims-warehouse`, but its `authentication` is unknown. If that unknown resolves to no verified and least-privileged writer identity, a party that can reach the warehouse write interface can inject or overwrite normalized claim rows outside `process:transform-job`. Second-order, `entity:data-analyst` queries the warehouse directly and may use altered member records, names, or dates of birth as legitimate analytics data. This claim is conditional on verification of the write caller being absent or insufficient.

mitigations.summary: Verify a dedicated transform writer identity
mitigations.detail: Configure `store:claims-warehouse` to accept writes only from a distinct authenticated workload identity for `process:transform-job`.

mitigations.summary: Constrain and audit warehouse write authority
mitigations.detail: Grant the transform identity only the required insert or partition-scoped operations, prevent arbitrary updates and deletes, and record immutable load provenance for reconciliation.

claims.title: Offline alteration of landing-bucket extracts is possible if at-rest protection is absent
claims.description: `store:landing-bucket` has `encryption_at_rest: unknown` despite holding confidential partner extracts containing health and PII data. If stored objects, snapshots, or restore media are not integrity-protected, an attacker with offline storage access can plant or alter an extract before it is restored or read. Second-order, `process:ingest-scheduler` reads every available file without verifying its originating partner, and `process:transform-job` can load the altered records into `store:claims-warehouse`. This claim is conditional on the unverified at-rest protection state.

mitigations.summary: Protect landing objects and recovery media at rest
mitigations.detail: Enable managed encryption covering `store:landing-bucket` objects, snapshots, and backups, with keys and restore permissions separated from ordinary ingest access.

mitigations.summary: Verify object integrity and provenance on ingest
mitigations.detail: Require a partner-signed manifest and object digest before `process:ingest-scheduler` or `process:transform-job` accepts a landing-bucket file.

claims.title: Offline alteration of Airflow metadata can redirect ingest behavior
claims.description: `store:airflow-metadata-db` holds Airflow connection strings and partner SFTP keys, is classified confidential, and has `encryption_at_rest: unknown`. If at-rest protection and restore integrity are absent, an attacker with offline access can alter stored connection configuration or partner key material before the metadata database is restored or used. Second-order, `process:ingest-scheduler` can be redirected to attacker-controlled sources or use substituted connection settings when it reads `flow:ingest-scheduler-to-airflow-metadata-db:read-connections`, changing which files it processes and sends onward to `process:transform-job`. This claim is conditional on the unverified at-rest protection state.

Airflow keeps its connection
strings and the partner keys in its own metadata database.

I don't know how the landing bucket is encrypted or whether the Airflow
metadata database is encrypted at rest.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional on the unknown at-rest and metadata-read protections because the attacker needs offline media access or a compromised restoration path. Impact is high because `store:airflow-metadata-db` contains `credentials` and `secrets`; altered scheduler configuration can redirect a business-critical ingestion process and poison downstream warehouse data.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and integrity-protect Airflow metadata and backups
mitigations.detail: Protect `store:airflow-metadata-db`, including snapshots and restores, with managed encryption, restricted key access, and verified backup integrity before restore.

mitigations.summary: Treat connection configuration as signed, reviewed code
mitigations.detail: Require versioned, reviewed changes and cryptographic verification for scheduler connection definitions and partner-key references before `process:ingest-scheduler` uses them.

mitigations.summary: Use short-lived partner access credentials
mitigations.detail: Replace stored long-lived partner SFTP keys with scoped, rotatable credentials so altered or recovered metadata is less useful to an attacker.

claims.title: Offline warehouse corruption may be accepted by direct analysts
claims.description: `store:claims-warehouse` is confidential, holds member claim records, and has `encryption_at_rest: unknown`. If warehouse storage, snapshots, or restored exports are not integrity-protected, an attacker with offline access can alter normalized claim records before they are restored or queried. Second-order, `entity:data-analyst` queries `store:claims-warehouse` directly under a dataset-wide grant and can make decisions from records whose member names, dates of birth, or claim values were changed. This claim is conditional on the unverified at-rest protection state.

quotes.text: Analysts query the warehouse directly.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional on `unknown:store:claims-warehouse:encryption_at_rest` because exploitation requires offline access to storage, snapshot, export, or restoration media. Impact is high because the store is confidential and tagged `pii`, `health`, and `business-critical-data`, and its records are directly consumed by analysts.

mitigations.summary: Protect warehouse data and backups with verified encryption
mitigations.detail: Apply managed encryption to `store:claims-warehouse` and all snapshots, exports, and backups, and verify integrity and provenance before any restore or import.

mitigations.summary: Detect unauthorized record changes
mitigations.detail: Maintain immutable load manifests, versioned partitions, and reconciliation checks so analysts can distinguish restored or loaded data from unauthorized modifications.

claims.title: Disputed warehouse loads may not be attributable to an individual actor
claims.description: An insider operating `process:transform-job`, or an attacker who gains that internal execution position, can cause normalized claim rows to be written through `flow:transform-job-to-claims-warehouse:load-records` and later deny initiating the load or being responsible for its contents. The flow's `authentication` is unknown, and the model contains no audit element or dedicated audit flow showing that a verified acting principal, action, target, timestamp, and outcome are retained. If this unknown resolves to a service-only or absent identity without an independent audit trail, `store:claims-warehouse` cannot rebut a dispute over who loaded or changed health-related claim records. Second-order: `entity:data-analyst` queries the warehouse directly, so disputed records may affect analytics and claims decisions while the organization cannot establish which actor introduced them. This finding is conditional on the unstated authentication and audit-recording design; it does not assert that no audit logging exists in deployment.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown authentication on `flow:transform-job-to-claims-warehouse:load-records`: `process:transform-job` is internal, so exploitation requires an insider position or compromise, but the model states no verified principal for the write. Impact is high because `store:claims-warehouse` is confidential and holds `pii`, `health`, and `business-critical-data`; inability to attribute disputed writes can affect the full normalized claims dataset.

mitigations.summary: Create an auditable identity-bound warehouse-load trail
mitigations.detail: Have `process:transform-job` emit structured, append-only audit events for every load, recording the verified initiating principal, workload identity, source file, affected target, timestamp, outcome, and correlation ID to a dedicated audit destination.

mitigations.summary: Use and propagate a verified workload and initiating identity
mitigations.detail: Resolve the unknown authentication on `flow:transform-job-to-claims-warehouse:load-records` with a unique workload principal, and propagate the scheduler or authorized operator identity that initiated each transform run so warehouse records do not identify only a generic job.

mitigations.summary: Preserve change history for claim rows
mitigations.detail: Configure `store:claims-warehouse` load and change history to retain before/after provenance and make corrections new attributable entries rather than untraceable overwrites.

claims.title: Landing-bucket extracts may be readable from storage media if at-rest encryption is absent
claims.description: `store:landing-bucket` is a confidential store holding health and PII claim extracts, but its `encryption_at_rest` is unknown. If storage encryption is not enabled, an attacker or over-privileged storage operator who obtains an operational copy of the bucket's media, snapshot, or export can read the partner extracts without using the SFTP upload path. The disclosed member identities and dates of birth can be correlated with records later loaded through `flow:transform-job-to-claims-warehouse:load-records`. This is conditional on the unverified at-rest encryption setting, not an assertion that encryption is absent.

quotes.text: The extracts contain claim records with member names and dates of birth.
I don't know how the landing bucket is encrypted

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `unknown:store:landing-bucket:encryption_at_rest` leaves the storage-layer control unverified, while obtaining an operational copy still requires storage-layer access. Impact is medium because the store contains health-related claim records with member names and dates of birth.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce bucket encryption at rest
mitigations.detail: Establish the actual encryption posture of `store:landing-bucket`, require managed-key encryption for the bucket and its operational copies, and restrict export, snapshot, and storage-admin access.

claims.title: Airflow metadata storage may expose partner keys and connection strings at rest
claims.description: `store:airflow-metadata-db` holds connection strings and partner SFTP keys and has `encryption_at_rest: unknown`. If the database or its operational copies are unencrypted, a person obtaining a database volume, backup, or export can recover these credentials without accessing `process:ingest-scheduler`. The recovered partner keys can then enable access to the partner upload path `flow:insurance-partner-to-landing-bucket:push-daily-extract` and its health and PII extracts. This threat is conditional on the unverified encryption-at-rest setting.

quotes.text: Airflow keeps its connection strings and the partner keys in its own metadata database.
or whether the Airflow metadata database is encrypted at rest.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and tightly control metadata-database copies
mitigations.detail: Verify encryption for `store:airflow-metadata-db`, enforce KMS-backed encryption for database storage, backups, snapshots, and exports, and limit key-use and export permissions.

mitigations.summary: Move and rotate partner credentials
mitigations.detail: Store SFTP keys in a dedicated secret manager with workload-scoped retrieval, rotate the longstanding partner keys, and avoid retaining plaintext connection secrets in broadly accessible metadata copies.

claims.title: Claims warehouse data may be readable from an unencrypted storage copy
claims.description: `store:claims-warehouse` is confidential and contains normalized health and PII claim records, while `encryption_at_rest` is unknown. If this unknown resolves to unencrypted storage, an attacker or over-privileged storage-layer principal who obtains an operational copy can read the warehouse directly rather than going through `flow:data-analyst-to-claims-warehouse:run-queries`. quotes.text: The transform normalizes the records and loads them into BigQuery.

Impact is high because the confidential warehouse holds normalized `pii` and `health` claim records, allowing corpus-scale and irreversible disclosure.

mitigations.summary: Verify warehouse encryption and protect all operational copies
mitigations.detail: Confirm the at-rest encryption posture of `store:claims-warehouse`; require KMS-controlled encryption for warehouse storage, exports, backups, snapshots, and replicas, with least-privilege decrypt and export permissions.

claims.title: Partner extract files may be intercepted on the scheduler read path

If transport protection is absent or terminates before this segment, an attacker with a foothold on the landing-network path can intercept the files as `process:ingest-scheduler` reads them. The exposed records are subsequently normalized and sent toward `store:claims-warehouse`. This is conditional on the unverified transport setting.

mitigations.summary: Require authenticated encryption on the bucket read path
mitigations.detail: Configure TLS for the object-storage API used by `flow:ingest-scheduler-to-landing-bucket:list-and-read-files`, validate the service endpoint, and use workload identity or mTLS for the scheduler-to-storage connection.

claims.title: Connection strings and partner keys may be intercepted between Airflow and its metadata database
claims.description: `flow:ingest-scheduler-to-airflow-metadata-db:read-connections` carries connection strings and partner SFTP keys from `store:airflow-metadata-db` to `process:ingest-scheduler`, but both its authentication and encryption in transit are unknown. If transport protection is absent, an attacker able to observe the landing-network database path can intercept standing credentials. Those credentials can then be used to reach the partner upload route `flow:insurance-partner-to-landing-bucket:push-daily-extract` and the sensitive claim extracts it carries. This is conditional on the unverified transport control.

quotes.text: Airflow keeps its connection strings and the partner keys in its own metadata database.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the two unverified controls on `flow:ingest-scheduler-to-airflow-metadata-db:read-connections` require an attacker to first obtain an internal on-path position. mitigations.summary: Encrypt and mutually authenticate the metadata-database connection
mitigations.detail: Require TLS with certificate validation, preferably mTLS, on `flow:ingest-scheduler-to-airflow-metadata-db:read-connections`, and replace unknown connection authentication with a workload-scoped database identity.

mitigations.summary: Eliminate long-lived recoverable partner keys from routine reads
mitigations.detail: Use a secret manager with short-lived, workload-bound secret retrieval and rotate the static partner SFTP keys so intercepted values have limited utility.

claims.title: Normalized claim records may be intercepted while loading the warehouse
claims.description: `flow:transform-job-to-claims-warehouse:load-records` transfers normalized claim records from `process:transform-job` to `store:claims-warehouse`, with `encryption_in_transit: unknown`. If this warehouse-network API segment lacks effective transport encryption, an attacker with an on-path foothold can intercept health and PII records during each load. The captured data supplies the same member-level information that analysts later retrieve directly from the warehouse. This threat is conditional on the unverified transport setting.

quotes.text: The transform normalizes the records and loads them into BigQuery.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional on `unknown:flow:transform-job-to-claims-warehouse:load-records:encryption_in_transit`, since an attacker must obtain an internal warehouse-network on-path position. Impact is medium because the flow carries normalized health and PII claim records, although the model does not establish that one load contains the entire warehouse corpus.

mitigations.summary: Enforce encrypted service-to-warehouse transport
mitigations.detail: Require TLS with endpoint validation for the BigQuery API connection on `flow:transform-job-to-claims-warehouse:load-records` and use a workload-specific authenticated identity for `process:transform-job`.

claims.title: Dataset-wide analyst access exposes member-identifying claim data beyond column need
claims.description: An honest-but-curious or compromised `entity:data-analyst` can use `flow:data-analyst-to-claims-warehouse:run-queries` to read member-identifying health claim data from `store:claims-warehouse` because the stated SSO grant is dataset-wide with no column-level restriction. This allows analysts who only need aggregate analytics to retrieve identifying columns directly. The disclosed identities and dates of birth can be retained or correlated outside the warehouse, making the confidentiality loss persist beyond the query session.

quotes.text: Analysts query the warehouse directly. They are on the warehouse network and authenticate with SSO, but the grant is dataset-wide — we have not split member-identifying columns out.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because `entity:data-analyst` is an authenticated internal principal and the stated dataset-wide grant makes direct querying routine, though use requires that granted access or compromise of it. Impact is high because `store:claims-warehouse` holds confidential health and PII claim records with member-identifying columns, and a dataset-wide query can disclose data at broad scale.

mitigations.summary: Restrict analyst access to minimum necessary fields
mitigations.detail: Replace the dataset-wide grant on `flow:data-analyst-to-claims-warehouse:run-queries` with role-specific views or authorized datasets that omit member-identifying columns unless a documented use case requires them.

mitigations.summary: Authorize and monitor sensitive query access
mitigations.detail: Apply column- and row-level controls to `store:claims-warehouse`, use separate reader principals for different analyst roles, and alert on bulk extraction or queries selecting identifying fields.

claims.title: Warehouse query results may be intercepted if analyst transport is not protected
claims.description: `flow:data-analyst-to-claims-warehouse:run-queries` returns claim records including member identifiers, while its `encryption_in_transit` value is unknown. If the analyst-to-warehouse API channel is not effectively encrypted, an attacker with a position on the warehouse-network path can intercept query requests or responses containing health and PII records. This can expose whatever broad dataset results the analyst retrieves from `store:claims-warehouse`, without requiring the attacker to authenticate as that analyst. The threat is conditional on the unknown transport state.

quotes.text: Analysts query the warehouse directly.
the grant is dataset-wide — we have not split member-identifying columns out.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional on `unknown:flow:data-analyst-to-claims-warehouse:run-queries:encryption_in_transit`, because interception requires an internal warehouse-network on-path position. Impact is high because the flow can return dataset-wide claim results containing member-identifying health and PII data.

mitigations.summary: Require encrypted analyst-to-warehouse connections
mitigations.detail: Enforce TLS with certificate validation for `flow:data-analyst-to-claims-warehouse:run-queries` and prevent plaintext or downgrade-capable client connections.

mitigations.summary: Reduce sensitive data returned over analyst queries
mitigations.detail: Use restricted views and column-level policy on `store:claims-warehouse` so routine analyst responses do not include member-identifying fields.

claims.title: Partner upload flooding can overwhelm nightly ingestion
claims.description: A malicious or compromised `entity:insurance-partner` can use its long-lived key on `flow:insurance-partner-to-landing-bucket:push-daily-extract` to flood `store:landing-bucket` with many or oversized schema-valid extracts. The attacker spends uploads while `process:ingest-scheduler` lists and reads every file and starts one `process:transform-job` run per file; input-size, object-count, and per-partner quotas are not stated in the model. Second-order, this turns the landing bucket into a workload amplifier: scheduler capacity and Spark capacity are consumed by attacker-supplied files, delaying legitimate partners' nightly extracts and their loads into `store:claims-warehouse`.

quotes.text: Each partner has a static key we issued when they onboarded; the keys have not changed since.
For each file the scheduler triggers a Spark transform job in the warehouse network.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium: `flow:insurance-partner-to-landing-bucket:push-daily-extract` crosses from `boundary:partner-network`, but exploitation requires a partner key or compromise of a partner holding one; the static keys are stated to be unrotated. Impact is medium: flooding `store:landing-bucket` can consume the nightly processing capacity of `process:ingest-scheduler` and `process:transform-job`, delaying the business-critical claims pipeline, but the stated harm is a recoverable batch-processing outage.

mitigations.summary: Enforce per-partner upload and storage quotas
mitigations.detail: Apply authenticated per-partner limits on object count, object size, total daily bytes, and upload concurrency on `flow:insurance-partner-to-landing-bucket:push-daily-extract`; reject excess data before it consumes `store:landing-bucket` capacity.

mitigations.summary: Bound scheduler fan-out and transform workload
mitigations.detail: Make `process:ingest-scheduler` process a bounded number of files per run, queue excess work with backpressure, and cap concurrent `process:transform-job` executions so one partner cannot translate uploads into unbounded Spark work.

mitigations.summary: Rotate and constrain partner credentials
mitigations.detail: Replace never-rotated static partner keys with individually managed, rotated credentials and revoke a partner credential promptly when abnormal upload volume is detected.

claims.title: Warehouse query flooding can consume shared BigQuery capacity
claims.description: An attacker who is an authorized `entity:data-analyst`, or who compromises that analyst's SSO session, can flood `flow:data-analyst-to-claims-warehouse:run-queries` with concurrent or deliberately expensive queries against `store:claims-warehouse`. The analyst has a dataset-wide grant and queries the warehouse directly; query concurrency limits, bytes-scanned caps, cost budgets, and workload separation are not stated. Second-order, shared warehouse throughput or quotas can be exhausted before `process:transform-job` completes `flow:transform-job-to-claims-warehouse:load-records`, delaying both analyst access and nightly claim-record ingestion.

quotes.text: Analysts query the warehouse directly. They are on the warehouse network and authenticate with SSO, but the grant is dataset-wide

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium: the attacker needs an internal analyst identity or a compromised SSO session, but that identity directly reaches `store:claims-warehouse` through `flow:data-analyst-to-claims-warehouse:run-queries` and relevant workload controls are unstated. Impact is medium: `store:claims-warehouse` holds business-critical claim data and is also written by `process:transform-job`, so exhausted shared query capacity disrupts both analytics and the recoverable ingestion pipeline.

mitigations.summary: Apply per-identity query and cost budgets
mitigations.detail: Set concurrency, bytes-scanned, runtime, and cost limits for `entity:data-analyst` queries on `flow:data-analyst-to-claims-warehouse:run-queries`, with automatic cancellation and alerting for anomalous consumption.

mitigations.summary: Isolate ingestion from interactive analytics
mitigations.detail: Reserve or partition `store:claims-warehouse` capacity so interactive analyst queries cannot starve `flow:transform-job-to-claims-warehouse:load-records`; make the transform fail fast or retry with bounded backoff when capacity is unavailable.

claims.title: Unauthenticated scheduler-to-transform crossing could grant landing-zone callers warehouse write authority
claims.description: `flow:ingest-scheduler-to-transform-job:trigger-transform` crosses from `boundary:landing-network` to `boundary:warehouse-network` and its `authentication` is unknown. If `process:transform-job` accepts trigger requests without authenticating and authorizing the originating scheduler or request, an attacker with a foothold in the landing network can invoke the warehouse-zone transform surface despite lacking warehouse authority. The transform validates only schema before using `flow:transform-job-to-claims-warehouse:load-records` to load records, so the gained authority can be used to cause schema-valid attacker-controlled claim rows to reach `store:claims-warehouse`, which holds member-identifying health claim data. This is conditional on the unstated authentication and authorization enforcement for the crossing, not a claim that it is absent.

quotes.text: Nothing validates the row contents beyond the schema.
The extracts contain claim records with member names and dates of birth.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional: `crossing:flow:ingest-scheduler-to-transform-job:trigger-transform` gives a landing-to-warehouse path, but exploitation requires a landing-network foothold and the unstated authentication on that flow to be ineffective. Impact is high because the resulting authority reaches `store:claims-warehouse`, whose claim records include member names and dates of birth and are tagged `pii` and `health`.

mitigations.summary: Authenticate and authorize every scheduler-to-transform request
mitigations.detail: Require `process:transform-job` to verify a workload identity for `process:ingest-scheduler` on `flow:ingest-scheduler-to-transform-job:trigger-transform`, and authorize only the minimal trigger operation rather than relying on landing-network reachability.

mitigations.summary: Constrain the transform job's warehouse authority
mitigations.detail: Use a narrowly scoped, short-lived identity on `flow:transform-job-to-claims-warehouse:load-records` that can write only the intended ingestion dataset and cannot grant broader warehouse capabilities.
